Definition: from G68; wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce):--wild, raging.
BiblicalUsage: Agrios is wild — of the country, untamed. John the Baptist ate locusts and wild honey in the wilderness — Matthew and Mark both tell it; and Jude calls false teachers raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame. The word covers the wildness of the desert and the wildness of men who will not be tamed — and the story always shows which wildness God uses and which He judges.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word draws a line I need to see. The wild honey fed the prophet — but the raging waves are reserved for judgment, and the difference is whether the wildness submits to God or rages against Him.
